title: Fleetdesk rental management
alt: Actual Fleetdesk vehicle-level availability showing a blocked vehicle, its real synthetic reservation dates and an available vehicle quotation action
desc: See which vehicles fit a rental period, quote and allocate safely, then search and export the saved reservation records.
built: Turned the rental overview into a vehicle-level decision workspace: explain blocking periods, preselect an available vehicle into the tested quotation flow, and search/export exactly the shown historical snapshots.
why: A rental workspace must prevent two customers from being promised the same vehicle for overlapping dates, and keep the reviewed price clear when records change.
how: Choose dates and inspect each vehicle’s advisory availability, including actual confirmed periods that block it.
Quote an available vehicle with its dates already selected; confirmation retains the tested allocation and price rechecks.
Combine reservation status filters with snapshot search, then export exactly the displayed records and saved integer-cent quotations.
demonstrates: Business workflow design, transactional allocation, accessible decision support, data integrity and independently verified record exports.
caption: Real availability disclosure from the working app: confirmed blocking periods and available-vehicle actions come from the same synthetic records and shared rules as the quotation workflow.
result: Existing record workflows and new rental workflows pass API/domain, browser-rule and full browser checks before this release. The isolated MySQL integration verifies simultaneous overlap rejection, retry identity, saved prices, referential integrity and state transitions. Desktop/mobile captures match this exact source revision; the linked run records its actual result.
limits: Synthetic educational application, with no real fleet, payments, tax/deposit calculation or deployed multi-user backend. The public demo is local to one browser profile and uses Web Locks to coordinate its tabs; it cannot allocate across devices. UTC dates use an exclusive return date. Early-return pricing, rental amendments and deletion of referenced history are outside scope. MySQL allocation safety assumes writes use the transactional service.
technical: Separate pure rental rules, memory/MySQL adapters and a presentation module preserve original CRUD routes. Python and JavaScript follow a 27-case rules contract. Memory uses a shared RLock; browser writes use an exclusive Web Lock and fresh storage read; MySQL confirmation locks the vehicle/customer rows in a transaction and preserves references with foreign keys. Request IDs prevent duplicate creation after a lost response. Integer-cent rate and name snapshots preserve quoted terms; stale rates require a new quote. The read-only availability roster delegates to those existing rules. Snapshot search and CSV formatting are isolated presentation helpers, independently checked with Python CSV parsing. Eleven browser journeys cover both Flask/static frontends, exact exports, keyboard focus and mobile decisions; all original MySQL contention checks remain.
run: Install requirements.txt; set DEMO_MODE=1 and run python CarServer.py. The README documents the non-destructive MySQL reservation migration and opt-in isolated integration checks. The public static demo shares its frontend and tested rules contract.

Search and CSV exports use preserved reservation snapshots, so current customer edits cannot silently rewrite history or quoted totals.

title: Breast cancer classification
alt: Actual saved-prediction comparison: logistic regression and random forest each make ten errors, sharing four, with anonymous source-row evidence
desc: Compare which saved examples classifiers miss together or separately, with exact row evidence and clear evaluation limits.
built: Extended the existing read-only results lab with paired error partitions and anonymous source-row evidence for all three classifiers and the training-majority baseline.
why: Two approaches can have the same error total while missing different examples. Aggregate scores alone cannot show that overlap; the saved predictions make it inspectable.
how: Reproduce the fixed evaluation and reconcile saved predictions with source labels, exact partitions, confusion counts and scores; training and model settings remain unchanged.
Choose approaches A and B to partition the same 171 holdout rows into both wrong, only A wrong, only B wrong and both correct.
Inspect anonymous source positions, actual labels, both predictions and explicit false-positive/false-negative outcomes for any group; no control trains or tunes a model.
demonstrates: Reproducible error analysis, independent reconciliation of paired observations, class-imbalance interpretation and accessible evidence exploration.
caption: Actual browser capture of the saved-results lab after desktop and mobile checks. The controls select previously computed outputs; they do not train a model.
result: Saved predictions from the unchanged three-model evaluation reconcile with source labels and confusion counts. Logistic regression: 7 missed / 64, Decision tree: 10 missed / 64, Random forest: 6 missed / 64. The training-majority baseline scores 62.6% accuracy but misses 64 of 64 malignant-labelled holdout examples. The explorer reports positive-class precision/recall/F1 and balanced accuracy without retraining. This repeatedly reused holdout is exploratory, with no independent or clinical validation. Logistic regression and random forest each make 10 and 10 saved errors respectively: 4 shared errors, 6 logistic-only errors and 6 forest-only errors. Paired counts describe these same rows; they are not a significance test or a new performance estimate.
limits: Educational analysis of a public teaching dataset, not a diagnostic system. This browser reads saved results only; it accepts no patient inputs and trains no models. The holdout has been reused across models and portfolio iterations, so it is exploratory rather than an untouched final test or an unbiased selection estimate. The baseline is context, not a new tuned classifier. No independent cohort, clinical validation, calibration study or causal feature interpretation is claimed.
technical: The Python exporter verifies source and prediction hashes, partition membership, labels and existing confusion/metric artifacts before exporting anonymous row positions and all sixteen ordered paired partitions. A training-majority baseline uses training labels alone. Independent pandas masks reconcile every partition, error marginal, row identity and swapped/self comparison. Browser tests reconcile every pair/group directly with the source prediction CSV at desktop/mobile widths, including outcome labels, empty states and keyboard selection. Existing training-only CV, split, models and evaluation code are unchanged.
run: Install requirements.txt, run python evaluate.py, python -m unittest discover -p "test_*.py" -v, python plot_portfolio.py and python build_explorer.py. Serve docs/ with a local static server. npm ci and npm run test:browser run repeatable desktop/mobile checks. The original notebook remains separate.

Native approach/group selectors and readable count cards on mobile; the evidence table scrolls within its labelled region.

challenge: Equal aggregate accuracy can conceal different mistakes. The paired explorer must compare the same rows in the same order, preserve the training-only baseline and distinguish wrong predictions by their actual labels. Source validation precedes partitioning, and every displayed group can be traced back to the saved CSV without exporting identifiers or feature measurements. Descriptive overlap is explicitly separated from significance testing or new unbiased performance claims.

title: Hotel booking prototype
alt: Verified room comparison for six synthetic guests: full three-night costs and explicit room-quantity recovery
desc: Compare full-stay room costs, resolve capacity limits and complete a recoverable demonstration booking.
built: Extended the existing Express/static booking journey with full-stay room comparisons and explicit quantity recovery, using the same exact-cent rules that validate the final quotation.
why: A nightly price alone hides the cost of a multi-room stay. Guests also need to understand why a room type cannot accommodate their party and how to correct the selection.
how: Choose future dates and guest count. Compare the full stay price for each room type, with its nightly rate, nights and room quantity shown.
Use an explicit minimum-room action to resolve capacity or stock problems; every comparison updates together, while previous quotes and reviews are invalidated.
Choose a room, enter sample details and review the exact same quotation. Existing session recovery and stable confirmation retries remain available.
demonstrates: Shared business rules, exact pricing, accessible recovery from invalid selections and consistent state across a multi-step application.
caption: Genuine capture of the verified shared interface. The hotel is fictional; photography is illustrative and credited. Browser-only public mode is labelled prominently.
result: Rule/API regressions, a disposable MySQL 8.4 catalog check and nine Express/static browser journeys gate publication. A six-guest, three-night example moves explicitly from one invalid double room at EUR360 to three valid rooms at EUR1080; these are synthetic quoted amounts, not bookings or business impact. Tests reconcile every room-card total with the later quote, clear stale downstream state after quantity changes, retain sample guest details, and check keyboard/mobile use alongside the existing confirmation recovery paths.
limits: The hotel, rooms, prices and guest records are synthetic. Public Pages runs only the shared browser demonstration; it does not run Express or MySQL. Stock is illustrative per room type, not a date-based hotel inventory or a held allocation. Confirmations create no real reservation, payment, account or message. Review/receipt state is temporary; the bounded Express cache and local session store are educational rather than a production booking database.
technical: A shared pure roomOption assessment computes integer-cent totals, capacity, stock eligibility and a bounded minimum-room suggestion. makeQuote delegates to that assessment and retains its original valid quote contract and rejection messages. Both manual and suggested quantity changes clear quote/review/receipt state while retaining dates and sample guest details. The server recalculates from its own catalog. Existing CSRF, 15-minute reviews, bounded token-keyed receipts and explicit stale-review recovery remain in place.
run: Run npm ci, npm test and npm start for Express at http://127.0.0.1:3000. No database is needed by default. npm run build:demo generates the public static version. An optional isolated MySQL Docker setup and opt-in integration test are documented separately.

challenge: Room cards and final quotation previously had separate eligibility calculations, and changing quantity could leave an older review reachable. One shared assessment now drives comparison and authoritative validation; one quantity-change boundary invalidates all downstream state. An invalid current quantity can show a clearly labelled price without enabling booking, and a repair is offered only when the required quantity fits example stock.

title: Plant growth & statistics
alt: Genuine PlantGrowth chart with all thirty measurements, selectable mean-plus-minus-SD bars and exact group endpoints
desc: Switch between observed spread and uncertainty in a mean, with the same thirty measurements and auditable bar endpoints.
built: Extended the existing PlantGrowth comparison lab with a native chart-bar selector that makes individual spread and uncertainty in a group mean visibly distinct.
why: Error bars can look similar while answering different questions. Visitors need to see what changes between sample variation and uncertainty about a mean without mistaking either for a treatment recommendation.
how: Inspect all thirty original observations. Switch the bars between mean ± one sample SD and pointwise 95% t intervals for each mean.
Read the exact active endpoints in the group summaries; the point positions, observations and common axis scale stay unchanged.
Compare the three existing Welch mean differences and Bonferroni-adjusted intervals separately. Changing the bars never changes the statistical method or pairwise results.
demonstrates: Clear statistical communication, reproducible observed-data visualisation, independent numerical checks and accessible interaction design.
caption: Actual shared-data chart in spread mode: circles are original measurements, diamonds are sample means and bars span mean ± one sample SD. Horizontal offsets only separate points. The uncertainty mode shows explicitly pointwise 95% mean intervals instead.
result: Thirty source observations, ten per group. Sample means: control 5.032, treatment 1 4.661, treatment 2 5.526 (dataset units). Primary Welch omnibus p=0.0174; classic ANOVA p=0.0159 is a sensitivity analysis. All three Welch comparisons use Bonferroni adjustment. Treatment 2 minus Treatment 1: +0.865 dataset units, adjusted 95% interval 0.085 to 1.645, adjusted p=0.0279. The explorer preserves all measurements and methods. No practical-benefit threshold or general treatment effectiveness is established.
limits: Thirty observations in a teaching dataset do not establish universal treatment effectiveness. Independence and the original experimental design cannot be verified from the CSV alone. Mean intervals assume approximate normality; Welch inference is a small-sample approximation. A p-value is neither an effect size nor the probability that the null hypothesis is true. Methods were selected for this educational investigation, not preregistered confirmatory analysis.
technical: The existing shared analysis objects still feed Matplotlib figures and browser data. No analytical method, source row or saved comparison changes. A native radio group changes only the displayed group endpoints; both modes use a fixed scale that includes all observations and both sets of endpoints. Exact active endpoints and clear interpretation accompany the chart. Six existing Python checks independently reconcile source rows, SDs, mean intervals and Welch/Bonferroni results. Five browser journeys additionally calculate means, sample SDs and t-interval endpoints from the original CSV, inspect SVG coordinates, preserve every point, check unchanged pairwise output and exercise keyboard/mobile interaction.
run: Install requirements.txt, run python analyze_plants.py, python -m unittest discover -p "test_*.py" -v and python build_explorer.py. Serve docs/ with a local static server. npm ci and npm run test:browser run repeatable desktop/mobile checks. Original CSV, saved calculations and coursework remain available.

The same observations and scale in uncertainty mode, with pointwise 95% t intervals and exact endpoints.
releases/applied-statistics/ddaa7ac0dd99cfc00c78977341c6623e230f159e/mobile-spread.jpg

challenge: A spread bar and a confidence interval can be visually mistaken for the same claim. The interface changes only the bars while retaining the exact same points and scale, then names the active quantity and exposes its endpoints. The explanation separates observed variation from model-based mean uncertainty, avoids fixed-coverage claims for one SD, and keeps pointwise intervals distinct from the adjusted pairwise tests.

title: Sorting algorithms, measured
alt: Actual sorting trace with original-position markers and exact evidence of equal items changing relative order
desc: Track original items through sorting exchanges and inspect equal-value order, while keeping operation counts separate from runtime.
built: Extended the existing traces with immutable original item identities, optional position labels and observed equal-value order evidence on the same shared input.
why: Equal numbers look interchangeable in a sorting animation. Original positions reveal relative-order changes and help distinguish one observed result from a general stability guarantee.
how: Choose repeated values or a custom input, then enable original positions. Each # identifies a starting item, independent of its value or current rank.
Step through actual exchanges and inspect the original/current order of repeated values. Compare observed final order for the same input across three traces.
Keep operation totals separate from the preserved five-algorithm Python benchmark; original implementations and recorded measurements remain unchanged.
demonstrates: Algorithmic reasoning, immutable trace state, controlled examples, regression testing and accessible interactive teaching.
caption: Genuine browser capture with original positions enabled. Equal-item order follows actual exchanges. Counts are JavaScript trace operations, not measured Python runtime.
result: Five Python implementations passed correctness checks on 125 measured sorts: five identical seeded random samples at each size from 50 to 1,000. Median and IQR are calculated from saved raw measurements. Measurements were recorded on Windows-11-10.0.26300-SP0 with Python 3.12.2; unchanged algorithm hashes reuse those observations. The browser explorer compares complete key-comparison/index-swap totals for three actual traces on the same generated or validated custom input. Selecting a trace and resetting preserve its starting values. These operation counts and animation pace are separate from the recorded Python runtime measurements.
limits: Measurements cover random non-negative integer inputs from 50 to 1,000 in one recorded environment; they do not establish a universal ranking. IQR describes observed variation, not confidence. Rightmost-pivot recursive quicksort has adverse-input recursion limits. Radix supports non-negative integers and rejects booleans/fractions. The browser explorer ports only three approaches and limits inputs to 24 values; animation pace is unrelated to Python runtime.
technical: Every frame copies original identities alongside values. Real index-changing exchanges swap both; self placements change neither. A pure helper validates the permutation and compares repeated-value subsequences with their original order. Labels are one-based, while toggling retains the step and input. Dense labelled charts have readable minimum-width bars and keyboard scrolling. Seven Python tests preserve algorithms/cache provenance; eight Node tests reconcile every frame identity/value, independent snapshots and known reversals. Five browser journeys cover exact identities, evidence, keyboard toggling/scrolling and mobile fit alongside existing playback/custom-input checks.
run: Install requirements.txt; run python benchmark_portfolio.py, python plot_portfolio.py and python -m unittest discover -p "test_*.py" -v. Use --refresh to request new measurements. For browser verification, build Python fixtures and docs, npm ci, npm run test:trace and npm run test:browser.

title: Iris dataset exploration
alt: Actual Iris distribution explorer with all source observations and separate median/quartile summary strips
desc: Explore feature distributions with original observations, independently checked quartiles and consistent species filters and exports.
built: Extended the existing observation lab with a single-feature distribution view, auditable medians/quartiles and full-range summaries, preserving the scatter controls and original rows.
why: A scatter plot shows relationships, but makes the distribution of one measurement harder to inspect. A shared observed-data view connects centres and spread to the source rows behind them.
how: Choose the scatter or single-feature distribution view. Distribution uses the horizontal feature and explains why the vertical control is inactive.
Filter species while retaining fixed feature ranges. Inspect original points, medians, quartiles, full observed ranges and IQR; browser statistics are checked independently in Python.
Return to the scatter presets, inspect selected rows or export all four original features. View changes never replace or remove source observations.
demonstrates: Descriptive data storytelling, precise quantile definitions, independent numerical verification, accessible controls and source-data integrity.
caption: Genuine distribution-view capture: symbols are original observations at exact feature values, separated vertically for readability. Summary strips show Q1, median and Q3, with observed min/max whiskers. No repeated row is removed.
result: 150 supplied observations, 50 per species. Mean petal lengths: Setosa 1.462 cm, Versicolor 4.260 cm, Virginica 5.552 cm. Observed petal-length medians: Setosa 1.500 cm (Q1 1.400, Q3 1.575), Versicolor 4.350 cm (Q1 4.000, Q3 4.600), Virginica 5.550 cm (Q1 5.100, Q3 5.875). Setosa forms a distinct petal cluster in these observations; Versicolor and Virginica overlap. All four measurements and all species labels are observed data, not model predictions. Repeated measurement rows are retained; this descriptive teaching sample does not establish general classification performance.
limits: This is descriptive exploration of a small, familiar teaching dataset. Separation in these observations is not independent validation of a classifier or evidence of general performance. Pooled correlations mix species and do not establish causation. Identical measurement rows are retained because equality alone does not prove duplicate sampling. The supplied CSV is preserved; historical Iris variants differ in two documented observations.
technical: A pure browser helper computes Type 7 linear quartiles from a sorted copy, preserving row order. Python exports twelve distribution references using NumPy linear quantiles; standard-library inclusive quartiles independently reconcile them. Both plot modes share feature scales and species markers. Distribution points keep exact feature values; deterministic vertical offsets separate observations, and summary strips sit below them for clarity. Six Python, five Node and five browser checks cover source variants/repeats, quartiles and edge cases, actual SVG geometry for every feature/species, filters, fixed scales, all-feature CSV exports, keyboard controls and mobile layout. Generated build metadata remains untracked.
run: Install requirements.txt; run python explore_iris.py, python -m unittest discover -p "test_*.py" -v and python build_explorer.py. Run npm ci, npm run test:rules, npx playwright install chromium and npm run test:browser. Serve docs locally to explore.

The lab preserves every supplied row, states its linear quantile method, labels full-range whiskers and gives vertical offsets no numerical meaning. Independent Python and browser calculations agree, and filtering changes only the view and selected-row export.
